\begin{abstract}
Accurate interpretation of dental panoramic radiographs (Orthopantomograms,
OPGs) is difficult because early carious lesions and periodontal bone changes
are subtle, the projection geometry is complex, and interpretation quality
depends strongly on clinical experience. In routine practice, this can lead to
slow reading, missed findings, and inter-observer variability, particularly for
junior clinicians and students.

This Phase 2 report documents the current implementation status of a
tooth-centric dental AI system under development for OPG analysis. The target
system is an end-to-end pipeline that will detect teeth on the full OPG, assign
FDI numbers, and generate a structured tooth-wise report for caries and
periodontal bone loss. In the work completed so far, two major analysis
branches have been developed and evaluated independently. The caries branch is
implemented as a two-stage ResNet18 cascade on DENTEX tooth crops: Phase 1
performs binary caries versus no-caries classification, and Phase 2 separates
caries from deep caries. The periodontal branch is built on the Tufts dental
dataset and includes annotation parsing, corrected tooth bounding-box
conversion, asymmetric crop generation, overlap-based tooth-level labeling,
binary bone-loss classification, overlap-based severity classification, and an
exploratory CEJ-based estimation module.

The strongest result obtained in this phase is the binary bone-loss classifier,
which achieved a validation macro-F1 of 0.9233 with sensitivity 0.8305 and
specificity 0.9953 on the held-out Tufts validation split. The overlap-based
bone-loss severity model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.7208, while the caries
severity stage achieved a macro-F1 of 0.77 on the preserved validation output
from the collaborator's DENTEX notebook. In contrast, the CEJ-based heuristic
module remained clinically unstable on OPGs and is therefore retained as an
exploratory component rather than the primary severity estimator. End-to-end
integration, YOLO-based tooth detection, FDI-aware report generation, model
calibration, and explainability overlays are planned for the next phase.
\end{abstract}
